title: Thoryn example recipe
description: SSO-2871 (Phase 0, SSO-2872) — a declarative, in-boundary product example the CLI applies to the caller's own account using only supported product workflows. Recipes are DATA, not code: the CLI is the only executor. The `action`/`assert` enums are a CLOSED allowlist mapping to supported product APIs — this is what structurally enforces the CLAUDE.md product-boundary rule (a recipe cannot express a DB seed, a demo endpoint, or any unsupported shortcut).

id.description: Stable recipe identifier used on the command line (e.g. simple-signin).

summary.description: One-line description shown by `thoryn examples catalog`.

requires.description: Preconditions the CLI checks before applying the recipe.

params.description: Typed parameters resolved (interactively in guided mode) before execution and referenced by `{{name}}` placeholders in step inputs.

validate.description: A regex the resolved value must match.

secret.description: If true, the value is never echoed or written to a receipt.

steps.description: Ordered provisioning actions. Each maps to a supported product API; results are addressable as {{<step id>.<field>}} in later steps.

action.description: CLOSED allowlist — supported product APIs only. Widening this is a deliberate product decision, never a convenience.

with.description: Per-action inputs, forwarded to the supported product API. For `applications.create` (register-app) these are `displayName`, `clientType`, `grantTypes`, `scopes`, `redirectUris` (array of redirect URI strings) and the optional `postLogoutRedirectUris` (array of OIDC RP-Initiated-Logout post-logout redirect URI strings, same shape as `redirectUris`; SSO-2897). For `identity.registerUser` (SSO-2907 — provision a sign-in-able tenant user via product-api `POST /api/v1/users`, `tenant:users.write`) these are `email`, `password` (sets an initial credential so the user can sign in immediately), the optional `givenName` / `familyName` / `locale`, and `emailVerified` (set `true` to mark the account verified without an email round-trip). The created user's `id` and `email` are addressable as `{{<step id>.id}}` / `{{<step id>.email}}` in later steps. For `tenant.configureEmailProvider` (SSO-2917 — configure the workspace's bring-your-own SMTP transport via product-api `PUT /api/v1/email-provider`, `tenant:email.write`) these are the merge-upsert config fields `providerType`, `enabled`, `smtpHost`, `smtpPort`, `smtpUsername`, `smtpPassword` (write-only; mark the param `secret:true` so it is never echoed or written to a receipt), `transportSecurity`, `fromAddress`, `fromName`, `replyTo`; the resulting `providerType` / `configVersion` / `enabled` are addressable as `{{<step id>.providerType}}` / `{{<step id>.configVersion}}` / `{{<step id>.enabled}}`. For `clients.createMachine` (SSO-2950 — the as-code machine-client bootstrap; provisions a confidential `client_credentials` client via the SAME product-api `POST /api/v1/applications` call `thoryn clients create` makes, `tenant:applications.write`) these are `displayName`, `clientType` (must be `confidential`), `grantTypes` (must include `client_credentials`), and `scopes` (array). This is the ONLY allowlisted action permitted to surface a secret: the minted `client_secret` is routed EXCLUSIVELY through the CLI's `SecretIo` channel (a `--secret-file`, or a guarded/interactive stdout — exactly as `thoryn clients create`), and is NEVER written to the receipt, a step output (`{{...}}`), a log, or argv. The receipt records only the non-secret shape (`clientId` + granted `scopes`); only `{{<step id>.clientId}}` is addressable in later steps.

verify.description: Read-only assertions run after the steps; each must pass for the run to succeed and be recorded in the receipt.

teardown.description: Best-effort removal of what the steps created, executed in declared order (child-first: delete the app, then the workspace it lives in — SSO-2901).

assets.description: Recipe-relative asset paths (a runnable loopback relying-party app, docs).
